name: Small white butterfly
description: A pale, fluttering butterfly that drifts from flower to flower.

facts.text: Feeds on nectar from open, sunny flowers.
Rests with its wings closed, showing their pale green-grey undersides.
More flowering patches mean more butterflies at once.

hints.text: Something pale and fluttering might come to flowers in bloom.

name: Swallowtail butterfly
description: A large, striking butterfly with tailed hindwings. An uncommon visitor.

facts.text: Only visits gardens with plenty of flowers in bloom.
Its tailed hindwings give the swallowtail its name.

hints.text: A rarer butterfly might visit a garden that is full of flowers.

name: Bumblebee
description: A round, fuzzy bee that hums steadily between flowers.

facts.text: Arrives once a couple of flower patches are in bloom.
Carries pollen between flowers as it feeds.

hints.text: A humming visitor may come once more than one patch is in flower.

name: Ground beetle
description: A glossy, dark beetle that keeps to damp, sheltered places.

facts.text: Moves into natural shelters that are shaded and surrounded by cover.
Spends most of its time hidden, venturing out to forage nearby.

hints.text: Something small might hide in a shady pile of logs and leaves.
A shelter in shade, with plants close around it, suits ground beetles.

name: Wren
description: A tiny brown bird with a cocked tail and a surprisingly loud song.

facts.text: Visits well-placed, improved shelters to search for insects.
Wrens often build nests in log piles and dense cover.

hints.text: An improved shelter might tempt a small bird.
Wrens visit improved shelters in good spots, and love a nesting bundle.

name: Japanese white-eye
description: A small olive-green songbird with a bright white ring around each eye.

facts.text: Comes to gardens with established bamboo, where it rests and preens out of the wind.
A mature maple nearby makes it a more frequent visitor.
White-eyes often travel in pairs, chattering softly to each other.

hints.text: Some songbirds like tall, dense growth to rest in.
Two or more mature bamboo clumps might draw a small green songbird.
A mature maple near the bamboo makes white-eyes visit more often.

name: Red admiral
description: A velvety black butterfly with bold red bands and white wing tips.

facts.text: Feeds on tree sap and fallen fruit as well as nectar.
Often basks with its wings spread flat in the sun.

hints.text: Not every butterfly feeds on nectar. Some prefer sap.
A sap feeder filled with maple sap draws the red admiral.

name: Mason bee
description: A small, gentle solitary bee that seals its nest tubes with mud.

facts.text: Nests in hollow canes, one egg chamber after another.
Solitary bees rarely sting; there is no hive for them to defend.

hints.text: Hollow canes could make homes for a solitary insect.
An insect hotel, built from a shelter, is where mason bees nest.

name: Wood mouse
description: A bright-eyed mouse with big ears and a long tail, busy after dark.

facts.text: Stores seeds and nuts in hidden larders near its nest.
Prefers dense cover; it seldom crosses open ground.

hints.text: A deep, dry lodge of logs might suit a small mammal.
A log lodge, built from a shelter, draws wood mice.
